correctness.rationale: For t existing vertices, unchosen parents retain unit weight; total weight S_{t-1}=t+c sum_{j<t}j^alpha, so exact activation conditional probability p_t=(t-I_{t-1})/S_{t-1}. Conditioning yields mean and variance recursions, with negative feedback coefficient (1-1/S); independent finite Markov transition masses through n=250 stayed normalized to 2.22e-16. For alpha<=1, Lambda=sum t/S diverges with power/log rate and correction sum E I/S =o(Lambda). Bounded-increment martingale strong law and triangular array CLT (predictable quadratic variation ~Lambda; Lindeberg) prove a.s. count, Gaussian and variance. For alpha>1 summable expected hazards gives finitely many first selections. Expected late count asymptotic equals sum q_t; pair-probability bound <=q_s q_t and Bonferroni yield last-activation sharp tail and power moment cutoff. Conditional eternal-star survival yields infinite product. Finite program matches full-history recursions only, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The activated-parent count measures structural branching diversity and the time to the last newly activated branch, natural observables not determined by single-color marginals. The universal alpha=1 trichotomy, central-limit scales, positive star probability and sharp late-activation tail identify a substantive boundary in a growing reinforced graph family, rather than arbitrary finite enumeration.
